key_insight: The paper encodes time as a quantum variable with O(log N_t) ancilla qubits, allowing one circuit to evaluate equilibrium correlation functions for all time points in parallel.
engineering_relevance: This reduces repeated circuit construction and execution for dynamic observables, offering a more scalable path to Green's functions and other response calculations on quantum hardware.
method: Store time indices in O(log N_t) ancilla qubits.
Use a single quantum circuit to process all time points simultaneously.
Run the circuit only O(log N_t) times, yielding O(N_t log N_t) total resources in the large-system limit.
evidence_signal: The abstract states the method is proven optimal and demonstrated on the Green's function of a one-dimensional spinless Hubbard model.
watch_item: The approach still depends on fault-tolerant-looking resource scaling and may face practical overhead from ancilla control, circuit depth, and Hamiltonian simulation accuracy on near-term devices.
paper_title: Efficient Calculation of Equilibrium Correlation Functions
